[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Scuza** [CF 1742E · Scuza](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1742/E){rating="1200"}

"Longest prefix whose every element is $\le k$" hangs on one number: $\mathit{pm}[i] = \max(a_0, \dots, a_i)$, the **prefix maximum**. A prefix of length $i + 1$ is climbable iff $\mathit{pm}[i] \le k$ — and prefix maxima are non-decreasing *by construction*, even when $a$ itself bounces around. So the searchable monotone array this time is not a prefix **sum** of a sorted copy (that was @sec-bst-p3-a) but a prefix **max** of the original order, and the height she reaches is the prefix *sum* read at the found index. Two companion arrays, one bisect.

[Solved in full in @sec-bst-p3-b.]{.card-link}

:::
